chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Begin your meal with salt and end with salt, for the one who begins his meal with salt and ends with salt will be cured from seventy-two types of affliction, among them leprosy, insanity, and vitiligo.'
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of eating salt at the beginning and end of a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the medicinal and spiritual efficacy of salt, a practice deeply rooted in the Sunnah and emphasized by Shia scholars for its protective qualities against both physical ailments like leprosy and mental afflictions such as insanity. The specific mention of seventy-two diseases reflects the comprehensive nature of prophetic medicine (al-Tibb al-Nabawi), where simple dietary elements are viewed as divine remedies for holistic well-being.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>! O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Begin your meal with the salt and end with the salt, for the one who begins his meal with the salt and ends with the salt, would be cured from seventy-two types of affliction, from it being the leprosy, and the insanity, and the vitiligo’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said to ’Amir al- Mu’minin, ‘O Ali, begin taking your food with salt and end it with salt. One who begins taking his food with salt and ends it with salt remains safe from seventy-two kinds of troubles of which is leprosy, insanity and albinism.’”
